source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb (and glossary); 8.5; 9.4

main.t: A three-cornered wrist bone, third in the first row of carpal bones (triquetrum).

simpler.t: The triquetrum is a small wrist bone on the little-finger side.

deeper.t: At the wrist joint it meets the articular disc over the ulna, not bone.

facts.t: It is the third bone of the first row, counting from the thumb side.
The lunate is beside it on the thumb side. The hamate is below it.
The pisiform sits on its front surface.

simpler.t: It sits on the little-finger side of the wrist.

deeper.t: It is one of only three carpal bones that take part in the wrist joint.

items.name: Facet for the pisiform
items.t: A small surface on its front, where the pisiform sits.

items.name: Surface for the wrist joint
items.t: Its upper surface meets the articular disc over the ulna.

items.name: Surface for the hamate
items.t: Its lower surface meets the hamate at the midcarpal joint.

simpler.t: It is a small three-cornered bone that carries the pisiform on its front.

deeper.t: Ligaments join it to the other bones of its row, so the row works as a unit.

facts.t: It meets the fibrocartilage pad that spans the radius and the ulna’s styloid process.
It carries the pisiform, which forms the bump at the base of the hand.
Its joint with the hamate is part of the midcarpal joint, which helps the wrist move.

simpler.t: It helps the wrist move and holds the pisiform in place.

items.name: Wrist (radiocarpal) joint
items.t: It meets the articular disc over the ulna.

items.name: Articular disc
items.t: A pad of fibrocartilage between the lower ends of the radius and ulna.

items.name: Midcarpal joint
items.t: Its lower surface meets the hamate.

items.name: Lunate
items.t: Its neighbour on the thumb side, joined to it by ligaments.

simpler.t: It joins the lunate, the hamate and the pisiform, and the disc over the ulna.

facts.t: It forms by replacing a cartilage model with bone (endochondral ossification), like all limb bones except the clavicle.
Its single ossification centre appears at about the third year.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20). Gray’s 1918 (8.2) gives the third year (supporting only).

items.injury: A fall onto the outstretched hand.
items.damaged: A small chip of bone breaks off the back of the triquetrum: the second most common carpal fracture.
items.cannotDo: Use the wrist without pain on the back of the little-finger side.
items.why: Ligaments and nearby bones strike or pull on its back surface as the wrist is forced backwards.

items.injury: A twisting fall on the hand.
items.damaged: The articular disc between the ulna and the triquetrum tears.
items.cannotDo: Turn the forearm or grip without pain on the little-finger side.
items.why: The disc unites the lower ends of the radius and ulna, and the triquetrum presses on it.
items.check: OpenStax describes the disc; a tear of the disc in a fall is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20).

items.q: Explain how the triquetrum takes part in the wrist joint without touching the ulna.
model: The wrist joint is formed above by the radius and the fibrocartilage pad.
The pad spans the radius and the ulna’s styloid process.
The triquetrum meets this pad (the articular disc over the ulna).
The ulna itself does not touch any carpal bone.

items.q: Compare the triquetrum and the pisiform.
model: Both are in the first row, on the little-finger side.
The triquetrum is three-cornered and third from the thumb side.
The pisiform is pea-shaped and sits on the front of the triquetrum.
Only the pisiform anchors the flexor retinaculum.

items.q: Press the bump at the base of the palm, below the little finger. Predict what you feel, and what lies beneath.
model: It projects forwards from the front of the triquetrum.
The flexor retinaculum attaches to the pisiform.

check.stem: Which bone sits on the front of the triquetrum?
check.why: The small pisiform sits on the front of the triquetrum.

check.stem: What does the triquetrum meet at the wrist joint?
options: The articular disc over the ulna
The head of the ulna directly
check.why: It meets the fibrocartilage pad that spans the radius and the ulna’s styloid process.

check.stem: Which bone lies below (distal to) the triquetrum?
check.why: Its lower surface meets the hamate.
